name: LongRoPE: Extending LLM Context Window Beyond 2 Million Tokens
problem: Extending a 4K-context model to 2M tokens by uniform positional interpolation needs non-uniform treatment of RoPE frequencies, and naive uniform scaling wastes short-context quality.
mechanism: Non-uniform positional interpolation. Split RoPE dimensions into a high-frequency group and a low-frequency group; keep the high-frequency group close to the original (short) positions so local resolution is preserved, and apply aggressive interpolation to the low-frequency group where the long-range structure lives. Adds a progressive extension strategy: first fine-tune at 256k, then apply a SECOND positional interpolation to reach 2048k; and finally readjust LongRoPE at 8k to recover short-context performance. Only the positional embedding changes - architecture is untouched.
speedup_reported: NOT A THROUGHPUT CLAIM. The abstract's quantitative claims are about CONTEXT LENGTH and quality: an 8x extension in non-fine-tuning scenarios, and a 2048k context window via the two-stage progressive strategy, with models retaining the original architecture and reusing most pre-existing optimisations. The serving-relevant property is that reuse: because only the position encoding changes, no engine or kernel work is needed to deploy it.
